attempts.label: CRCNS:ret-1
attempts.entry_title: Retinal ganglion cell responses in Pcdh-gamma mutant retina (Lefebvre et al. 2008)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's central histology could not be tested, and the part that could be tested gave a mixed picture. The data set holds only white-noise spike recordings, so the paper's thinned retinal layers, extra apoptosis, Bax rescue and normal laminar targeting could not be tested, nor could the flashing-spot, flash and moving-stimulus responses of Figure 9A to 9C. Of the Figure 9 findings that could be tested, the slower time course and lower firing rate in mutant retina held up, while the unaltered threshold did not (mutant thresholds were higher). Similar receptive field size and reduced gain could not be settled, because the paper does not specify its band construction or its model's nonlinearity. The data set's unit counts also differ from the paper's (200 mutant and 122 control units against 115 and 143).
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Lefebvre, Zhang, Meister, Wang and Sanes (2008) on CRCNS data set ret-1, which holds multielectrode recordings of 325 units from 16 mutant and control mouse retinas stimulated with flickering bars and checkerboards. It compares receptive field size, response time course, firing rate and Linear-Nonlinear model threshold and gain between Pcdh-gamma mutant and control retinas (Figure 9D to 9H). The histology of Figures 1 to 8 and the flash, spot and grating experiments of Figure 9A to 9C are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Lefebvre et al. (2008), Figure 9, from CRCNS ret-1

The data set's labels give 200 mutant units (87 Chx10-Cre in 6 retinas, 113 Pax6-Cre in 4) and 122 control units (95 labelled "WT (chx10 het)" in 3 retinas, 27 "WT (pax6 het)" in 2), against 115 (103.5 to 126.5) and 143 (128.7 to 157.3). Every unit fired during the bar stimulus. Units whose STA peak exceeds 1.5 times the null's number 138 mutant and 113 control; above 2 times, 103 and 107. Neither mutant count shown is inside its tolerance (103 is just below 103.5), but the mutant count falls from 138 to 103 between the two thresholds, so a threshold between them could put it inside, and with the 20080702 frames as deposited the count above 1.5 is 126, inside it. No count of control units can exceed 122, so the counts miss under any reading of a flicker response because of the control count. Without the second unit of each duplicate pair, 189 and 118. The Bax -/- retina (3 units) is in neither group. The notebook tabulates the units per retina and label; the files do not give the region recorded in the Pax6-Cre retinas, so the paper's peripheral subset cannot be formed.
deviations: The claims file asks also for the count of units with a flicker response without defining one; the counts above two thresholds of the STA peak over a null STA are shown as a standard choice, and none can change the outcome.
The control retinas are as the data set labels them; 95 of the 122 control units carry a label ("WT (chx10 het)") that the paper's description of its controls does not include.

outcomes.notes: The data set holds no flashing-spot recordings; every recording is binary white noise (flickering bars or checkerboards). The claim also depends on fig9c-on-off-index, blocked for the same reason. The paper names no other deposit.
The On-Off index needs the flashing-spot experiment of Figure 9A, which is not in the data set; every recording is binary white noise.
The data set holds no flashes, dim or bright; every recording is binary white noise at one luminance range, so the criterion's pair of intensities is absent.
The data set holds no moving gratings or moving bars; every recording is binary white noise. It also depends on fig9a-response-variety, which is blocked.

The outcome rests on one borderline combination and on the frame correction of the 20080702 bar recordings. The readings disagree. In 17 of 18 combinations (3 recording readings, 2 separations, 3 bands) the 95% bands separate with mutant centres smaller; under reading B with the svd separation the DKW bands overlap (median 134 against 156 um, KS p = 0.004). Reading A, svd, median 122 against 156 um (KS p below 1e-4). This follows the correction of the frame of the 20080702 bar recordings; with the frames as deposited the reading B DKW bands separate too and all 18 separate, which was the outcome (not_reproduced) of the first run. Much of the difference comes from mutant units with weak STAs (97 of 200 mutant and 15 of 122 control units have an STA peak less than twice the null's). Among units above that, the medians are 145 and 158 um (reading A, KS p = 0.19), the binomial and bootstrap bands separate only between 82 and 101 um, and the DKW bands overlap; over the three readings 13 of 18 combinations separate in that subset, and 1 of the 6 DKW ones, so the outcome there is blocked too. With the 16.6 um bars alone 16 of 18 separate (the svd DKW bands overlap under readings A and B), and with Pax6-Cre mutants alone the svd DKW bands overlap under reading A. Under shuffled group labels the binomial and bootstrap bands of this measure separate in 38 and 45% of shuffles and the DKW band in none. The answer to the question in questions/crcns-ret-1.yaml (which bar recording) found that the paper does not say, and the criterion requires the outcome under the three recording readings A, B and C, which are run here.
deviations: All 5 retinas recorded with 8.3 um bars are mutant; every control retina was recorded with 16.6 um bars.
The mutant group cannot be restricted to the peripheral region of the Pax6-Cre retinas, as the data set does not say where they were recorded.
The vertical bars of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 are rebuilt with a frame of 16.6718 ms, the frame of the other bar recordings, not the stated 16.6691 and 16.6653 ms (see findings).

outcomes.notes: Under all 12 readings (3 recording readings, 2 separations, depths of 10% and 20%) at least one mutant and one control unit have a lobe of opposite sign on both flanks of b(x); reading A, svd, 20%, 90 of 200 mutant and 16 of 122 control units. The same rule applied to null STAs (spike counts shifted by half the recording) is met by 194 to 198 of 200 mutant and 119 to 121 of 122 control units, so the rule is met by noise. Among units with an STA peak above twice the null's, at least 7 mutant and 4 control units meet it at 20% in every reading. The outcome follows the criterion, but the result is no evidence for or against surrounds.
deviations: The vertical bars of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 are rebuilt with a frame of 16.6718 ms, as for fig9d-rf-size-similar.

outcomes.notes: In all 36 combinations (3 recording readings, 2 separations, 2 peak readings, 3 bands) the bands separate with the mutant curve at longer times, and in none do they separate the other way; mutant medians exceed control ones by 16.7 to 33.3 ms (reading A, svd, frame, 125 against 108 ms), KS p at most 6e-10. The DKW band, which never separated under shuffled labels, separates in every combination. The result holds in every variant, including units with clear STAs (103 mutant, 107 control), each Cre line alone and the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone under reading A, and among units with clear STAs, with 16.6 um bars alone and with the 20080702 frames as deposited under all three readings (36 of 36 separate in each). With the frames as deposited, 8 binomial and bootstrap combinations (peak separation, readings A and C) also hold 1 or 2 values where the bands separate the other way; with the frames corrected none do. The statement's "significantly" has no named test in the paper; the KS test is shown.
deviations: Lag j is placed at (j + 0.5) frames, the data set's example script's convention; the offset is the same for every unit.
The vertical bars of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 are rebuilt with a frame of 16.6718 ms, as for fig9d-rf-size-similar.

outcomes.notes: In all 9 combinations (3 recording readings, 3 bands) the bands separate with the mutant curve at lower rates, DKW included; reading A, median 3.82 against 9.02 Hz (ratio 0.42; 0.38 to 0.45 over readings). By retina, mutant medians 1.9 to 15.9 Hz, control 3.8 to 23.6 Hz. Every variant gives a lower mutant median; with Pax6-Cre mutants alone (ratio 0.68) and among units with clear STAs (0.66), the DKW bands overlap while the binomial and bootstrap bands separate (those two separate in 38 and 39% of label shuffles for this measure). With the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone (ratio 0.41) the DKW bands separate. The outcome depends on using all units, as the claims file's header reads the groups (all units of each group, the paper naming no exclusion). Among units with clear STAs, over the three readings, 6 of 9 combinations separate and no DKW one, which the criterion would call blocked. With the frames as deposited and with 16.6 um bars alone all 9 separate. The answer to the question in questions/crcns-ret-1.yaml (which bar recording) found that the paper does not say; the criterion requires the three recording readings A, B and C, with the pooled spike count and duration under B, as run here.

In all 36 combinations (3 recording readings, 2 fits, 2 forms, 3 bands) the bands separate, with mutant thresholds higher, DKW included; reading A, frame fit, median 1.12 against 0.44 SD of the generator (continuous form) and 1.69 against 0.01 (printed form). Part of this comes from mutant units with weak STAs, whose generator predicts little of the rate; among units with clear STAs the medians are 0.86 against 0.41 (reading A, frame fit, continuous form), and over the three readings 24 of 36 combinations separate and no DKW one, which the criterion would call blocked. The outcome depends on using all units, as the claims file's header reads the groups. With the frames as deposited and with 16.6 um bars alone all 36 separate. The binned fit in the printed form stops at a grid edge in 107 of 200 mutant fits, all at the top, and 39 of 122 control fits, 33 at the top and 6 at the bottom (reading A); why they reach the top is not shown. Without the edge fits its medians are -0.03 and -0.03 (KS p = 0.21) and its DKW and bootstrap bands overlap, but that comparison drops most high mutant fits by construction and is no evidence that the threshold is unaltered. The frame fit in the continuous form has 1 fit per group at a grid edge, at the top, and separates under every band. With the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone the DKW bands still separate.
deviations: Theta is searched on 99 quantiles of y for the frame fit and at every split between the 20 bin centres for the binned fit, a standard choice of resolution; the binned grid cannot place theta above the last split, which many printed-form fits reach.
The vertical bars of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 are rebuilt with a frame of 16.6718 ms, as for fig9d-rf-size-similar.

outcomes.notes: The readings of the nonlinearity's form disagree. With the printed form (B + G y above theta), mutant gains are lower and the bands separate in all 18 combinations (reading A, frame fit, median 18.4 against 23.1 Hz per SD, ratio 0.80). With the continuous form (B + G (y - theta)), the bands overlap in 9 of 18, separate with mutant gains lower in 4 (reading B, binomial and bootstrap) and the other way in 5 (readings A and C); the DKW bands overlap in all 6 continuous-form combinations (reading A, frame fit, median 30.4 against 30.8, KS p = 0.76). Under reading B the continuous-form separations rest mostly on the 4 to 13 mutant gains below the lowest control gain, and under reading A, frame fit, bootstrap, on 1 mutant against 6 control cells; the others lie inside the distributions (reading A, binned fit, 165 of 200 mutant and 113 of 122 control cells at or below 41.46; reading C, frame fit, 16 to 19 mutant against 23 to 25 control cells near 21.2). Among units with clear STAs neither form gives lower mutant gains under reading A (printed 23.1 against 23.4, continuous 33.1 against 31.0); over the three readings in that subset the printed form separates with mutant gains lower in 6 of 18 combinations and the continuous form in 4, with 6 the other way and no DKW separation, so the outcome there is blocked too. With the frames as deposited the continuous form separates in 4 of 18, all with mutant gains lower, and the outcome is the same. On synthetic cells that follow the continuous form (theta 0.5, G 20), the printed-form frame fit returns theta 0.75 and G 13.4, so part of the printed-form gain reduction may mirror the higher mutant thresholds.
deviations: The vertical bars of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 are rebuilt with a frame of 16.6718 ms, as for fig9d-rf-size-similar.

findings.statement: The data set holds only the white-noise recordings behind Figure 9D to 9H. The histology of Figures 1 to 8 and Supplementary Figure 1, and the flashing-spot, flash, moving-bar and grating recordings of Figure 9A to 9C, are not in it, and the paper names no other deposit. Of the 26 claims, 19 cannot be tested.

The data set holds 200 mutant and 122 control units (and 3 from a Bax -/- mutant), where the paper's Figure 9 has 115 mutant and 143 control cells. The data set does not say how its units relate to the paper's, which were kept, or why the counts differ.

The data set labels 95 of its 122 control units "WT (chx10 het)", while the paper's Figure 9 legend gives the controls as Pax6-Cre;Pcdh-gamma +/f-del or Pcdh-gamma f-del/f-del without Cre. The labels and the paper disagree on what the controls were.

In the 8 recordings of 20080628_R4, 20080628_R6, 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4, 82 of 86 spike trains are not in time order. Each runs to 1440 s and then holds a second segment between 720 and 780 s, though the stimulus runs to 1500 s. The 4 trains in order have spikes between 1440 and 1500 s, about as many as between 720 and 780 s, and moving the segments by 720 s raises their STA peaks over the null in most units. This is consistent with the last minute stored with a 720 s offset in place of 1440 s. One checkerboard recording (20080628_R5) has 1 or 2 spikes near 2 s out of order in 15 units.

The frame lengths stated for the vertical-bar recordings of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 (16.6691 and 16.6653 ms) are not those of the stimulus. Rebuilt with the stated frame, the bars of 20080702_R4 give no STA above the null in any of its 12 units (median ratio 0.96), though all 12 respond to the checkerboard of the same retina. A scan of the frame peaks at 16.671 to 16.672 ms in both recordings; with 16.6718 ms, the frame of every other bar recording and half the checkerboard frame of the same two retinas, the median ratio is 2.57 and 10 of the 12 units have peaks above twice the null's.

16 pairs of units share 70 to 100% of their spikes within 0.5 ms in every recording of their retina (12 pairs in mutant retinas, 4 in a control retina), most likely single neurons sorted twice. The data set does not mark them.

The files do not give the age of the mice, the Pcdh-gamma allele (the paper's Results say fcon3 and its Figure 9 legend f-del), the region recorded in the Pax6-Cre retinas (the paper used their periphery only), or the cell type of the units.
